summary.text: Apple's FY2025 10-K organizes risks into macroeconomic/industry, business, legal and regulatory, and financial categories, emphasizing global supply-chain and international sales concentration, intense competition with minority market share, product-transition execution, and margin pressure from tariffs, FX and pricing.

Tesla's FY2025 10-K centers on growth-execution risk — production ramps of Cybercab/Robotaxi and AI-based autonomy, EV demand perception and cyclicality, product defects and largely self-insured product liability, and dependence on Elon Musk.

JPMorgan's FY2025 10-K enumerates a financial-institution risk taxonomy — legal/regulatory, political, market, credit, liquidity, capital, operational, strategic, country and people risks — with cyber attack, private-credit contagion and model/risk-framework failure highlighted.

Comparison: all three flag macro/geopolitical shocks, cybersecurity and data-privacy exposure and regulatory scrutiny, but Apple's and Tesla's are product, supply-chain and demand risks while JPMorgan's are balance-sheet risks (credit, liquidity, capital) tied to regulatory capital requirements; Apple's FY2026 Q1 10-Q reports no material change.

claims.text: Apple states its operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions, with sales outside the U.S. a majority of total net sales and a majority of supplier facilities located outside the U.S.
claims.quote: representing a majority of the Company's total net sales. In addition, the Company's global supply chain is large and complex and a majority of the Company's supplier facilities, including manufacturing and assembly sites, are located outside the U.S.

claims.text: Apple cites competitive risk, noting it has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets.
claims.quote: The Company has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets, and some of the markets in which the Company competes have from time to time experienced little to no growth or contracted overall.

claims.text: Apple flags net sales and gross margin volatility from pricing pressure, competition, supply shortages, component costs, FX, inflation and new or increased tariffs and retaliatory actions; it also notes a significant portion of net sales comes from a single product category.
claims.quote: the Company generates a significant portion of its net sales from a single product category and a decline in demand for that product could significantly impact net sales and gross margins.

claims.text: Apple identifies IT system failures, network disruptions and cybersecurity incidents, plus losses or unauthorized release of confidential personal information, as risks to its business and reputation.
claims.quote: Losses or unauthorized access to or releases of confidential information, including personal information, could subject the Company to significant reputational, financial, legal and operational consequences.

claims.text: Tesla's lead risk is issues or delays in developing, launching and ramping production, stating its future business depends on driver assistance and autonomous driving solutions and increasing production of mass-market vehicles including Cybercab, its Robotaxi product.
claims.quote: our future business depends on development of our driver assistance systems and autonomous driving solutions and increasing the production of mass-market vehicles, including Cybercab, our purpose-built Robotaxi product.

claims.text: Tesla notes electric vehicles still constitute a small percentage of overall vehicle sales and that demand may be affected by perceptions of range, charging access, competition, oil and energy price volatility and government incentives, with automotive sales tending to be cyclical.
claims.quote: In addition, electric vehicles still constitute a small percentage of overall vehicle sales. As a result, the market for our vehicles could be negatively affected by numerous factors

claims.text: Tesla discloses product defect, recall and product liability risk and states that in most jurisdictions it generally self-insures against product liability claims for vehicle exposure, so claims are paid from company funds.
claims.quote: In most jurisdictions, we generally self-insure against the risk of product liability claims for vehicle exposure, meaning that any product liability claims will likely have to be paid from company funds and not by insurance.

claims.text: Tesla identifies key-person risk, stating it is highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk and that none of its key employees is bound by an employment agreement for any specific term.
claims.quote: In particular, we are highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer. None of our key employees is bound by an employment agreement for any specific term

claims.text: JPMorgan's principal risk factors begin with legal and regulatory risks, including extensive supervision and regulation, changes in application or enforcement of law, litigation and investigation penalties, and losses absorbed by security holders in a resolution.
claims.quote: The principal risk factors include:•Legal and Regulatory risks, including the impact of extensive supervision and regulation, as well as changes to or in the application, interpretation or enforcement of applicable law or executive branch actions

claims.text: JPMorgan also lists political, market, credit, liquidity and capital risks, including effects of interest rates and credit spreads, collateral value declines, constrained liquidity, credit rating downgrades, and limits on capital distribution if regulatory capital requirements are not satisfied.
claims.quote: •Capital risks, including the risk that JPMorganChase's ability to distribute capital to shareholders or to support its business activities could be limited if it does not satisfy applicable regulatory capital requirements.

claims.text: JPMorgan's operational risks include dependence on operational systems and employees, harm from a successful cyber attack or other extraordinary events, data management and personal information safeguarding, vendor oversight, and its risk management framework and models.
claims.quote: •Operational risks, including risks associated with JPMorganChase's dependence on its operational systems and its employees... the harm that could be caused by a successful cyber attack affecting JPMorganChase or by other extraordinary events

claims.text: Apple's FY2026 Q1 10-Q reports no material changes to its risk factors since the 2025 Form 10-K.
claims.quote: There have been no material changes to the Company's risk factors since the 2025 Form 10-K.

claims.text: JPMorgan cites private-credit contagion risk, noting the significant expansion of private credit could worsen losses among non-bank lenders and borrowers, impair asset valuations and increase default rates.
claims.quote: the interconnectivity across credit markets increases the risk that the significant expansion of private credit could worsen losses among non-bank lenders and their borrowers, particularly if stress or defaults spread to broader funding and credit markets.

summary.text: NVIDIA's revenue base has expanded roughly fivefold in two fiscal years: FY2024 revenue was $60.9 billion, up 126% year over year, driven by a 217% increase in Data Center revenue.

FY2025 revenue reached $130,497 million versus $60,922 million in FY2024, with growth driven by data center compute and networking platforms and the start of Blackwell production shipments in Q4 FY2025.

Growth remains rapid but the year-over-year rate has moderated from triple digits: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $57,006 million versus $35,082 million a year earlier, and nine-month revenue was $147,811 million versus $91,166 million.
Management now attributes growth to three platform shifts (accelerated computing, powerful AI models, agentic applications) rather than the single Hopper generative-AI surge cited in FY2024.
The excerpts contain no forward revenue guidance figures, so the forward outlook is qualitative only.

summary.text: All five companies flag the same core regulatory exposures: extensive FDA and foreign approval requirements, government and payer price controls, and enforcement/compliance risk around marketing and pricing practices.

JNJ describes broad FDA administrative powers (recalls, seizures, withdrawal of approvals) plus rising compliance costs from new laws, and notes possible delays from reductions to the FDA's budget and personnel; its stated mitigation is to "identify, manage and mitigate risks" and to sustain innovation, with new products from the past five years at roughly 25% of 2025 sales.

Pfizer emphasizes payer/PBM formulary and rebate pressure plus ex-US price regulation, including the EU pharmaceutical legislation reform that may alter regulatory exclusivity periods and the EU HTA Regulation effective January 2025, which it says it is "engaging and monitoring."

Merck cites extensive FDA and foreign regulation and warns that elimination of FDA drug user fee programs could delay inspections and approvals, alongside government-mandated annual price cuts in Japan.

Lilly is most explicit on mitigation: in November 2025 it announced preliminary voluntary agreements with the U.S. government to lower Medicaid and certain other drug prices and to launch new medicines with more balanced pricing across developed nations, while flagging scrutiny of promotional practices and the FDA National Priority Voucher pilot.

AbbVie frames the risk as costly, time-consuming approvals and a highly regulated U.S. healthcare system subject to frequent change, compounded by government-mandated European price reductions and rebate programs.

claims.text: JNJ states that regulatory agencies have administrative powers to impose product withdrawals, recalls, seizures and civil and criminal sanctions, and that the FDA and global agencies are increasing enforcement activities.
claims.quote: The regulatory agencies under whose purview the Company operates have administrative powers that may subject it to actions such as product withdrawals, recalls, seizure of products and other civil and criminal sanctions.

claims.text: JNJ warns that new product development and regulatory approval may be delayed by limits on federal agency budgets or personnel, including reductions to the U.S. FDA's budget, employees and operations.
claims.quote: the development and regulatory approval of new products may be delayed due to limits on federal agency budgets or personnel, including reductions to the U.S. FDA's budget, employees, and operations, which may lead to slower response times and longer review periods

claims.text: JNJ's mitigation emphasis is continued innovation to offset revenue losses; new products introduced within the past five years accounted for approximately 25% of 2025 sales.
claims.quote: New products introduced within the past five years accounted for approximately 25% of 2025 sales.

claims.text: Pfizer identifies ex-US government price regulation in markets such as EU member states, the U.K., Japan, China, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, including China's QCE/VBP tender process causing significant price cuts for off-patent medicines.
claims.quote: In certain markets, such as in EU member states, the U.K., Japan, China, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, governments have significant power as large single payors to regulate prices, access criteria, or impose other means of cost control

claims.text: Pfizer notes the proposed EU pharmaceutical legislation reform may alter regulatory exclusivity periods, and says it is engaging with and monitoring the EU Health Technology Assessment Regulation that took effect in January 2025.
claims.quote: This reform may alter regulatory exclusivity periods for our products... with the European Regulation on Health Technology Assessment (EU HTA-R) taking effect in January 2025, we are engaging and monitoring application of the EU's new clinical assessment program

claims.text: Merck states its research, preclinical testing, clinical trials, manufacturing and marketing are subject to extensive regulation by the FDA and foreign authorities including in the EU, Japan and China, and that FDA requirements have increased time and resources to bring products to market.
claims.quote: The Company's activities, including research, preclinical testing, clinical trials and the manufacturing and marketing of its products, are subject to extensive regulation by numerous federal, state and local governmental authorities in the U.S., including the FDA, and by foreign regulatory authorities

summary.text: Bank of America's FY2024 10-K groups its material risk factors into categories, beginning with market risk from financial markets, fiscal, monetary and regulatory policies, and economic conditions, with volatility affecting interest rates, currencies, equity and commodity prices.

Credit risk is a second pillar: recessionary conditions, elevated rates and higher unemployment could impair consumer and commercial borrowers, with certain sectors such as commercial real estate (particularly office) singled out, and credit concentrations by industry, geography, product, asset class or counterparty could magnify losses.
Geopolitical risk covers political, economic, market, reputational, operational, compliance, legal and regulatory exposures across the jurisdictions in which it operates, including emerging markets.

Business operations risk centers on failure or breach of its own or third parties' operations and information systems, including cybersecurity incidents that the company expects to continue with increased frequency and severity.
The excerpts are qualitative only and the FY2025 Q3 10-Q refers back to this annual disclosure, so no updated or quantified risk exposures are available.

summary.text: NVIDIA reports two reportable segments — Compute & Networking (data center accelerated computing, networking, automotive/robotics platforms, DGX Cloud) and Graphics (GeForce, RTX/Quadro workstation, vGPU, Omniverse) — and in Q3 FY2026 they generated $50,908M and $6,098M of revenue respectively on $57,006M total.
For the first nine months of FY2026 the split was $131,828M Compute & Networking and $15,983M Graphics of $147,811M total, showing roughly 89% of revenue in the Compute & Networking segment.

On a full-year basis, FY2025 segment revenue was $116,193M Compute & Networking and $14,304M Graphics, consolidating to $130,497M, with an unallocated "All Other" category carrying only expenses (no revenue).

NVIDIA supplements segments with an end-market view, which in Q3 FY2026 was Data Center $51,215M (Compute $43,028M, Networking $8,187M), Gaming $4,265M, Professional Visualization $760M, Automotive $592M and OEM and Other $174M.
